draft.title: Perspectives and interpretations
card: how a person saw events at the time. It is shaped by who they were, such as their age, job, beliefs and what they stood to gain or lose.
a historian's explanation of the past, written later. It is built from many sources and tries to explain what happened and why.
Historians can reach different interpretations of the same events. They may use different sources, give some evidence more weight, or ask different questions.
Disagreement does not mean one historian is careless. Interpretations can be compared by asking what evidence each one uses and how well it supports the claim.
draft.remember: A perspective is a view from the time. An interpretation is a later explanation, and historians can differ.

a.q: Which of these is an interpretation of the past?
opts: A historian's 2015 book arguing why a strike began
A miner's letter describing the strike as it happened
A newspaper report written on the day of the strike
A worker's diary entry about her wages that week
a.why: An interpretation is a historian's later explanation, built from many sources. The letter, report and diary were made at the time, so they show the perspectives of people who lived through it.
a.clue: Look for the one written later by someone explaining the events.

b.q: Two historians study the same gold rush town. One argues it was mostly peaceful. The other argues it was often violent. What best explains this?
opts: They may use different sources or weigh evidence differently
One historian must have lived there and the other did not
Only one of them can be using real evidence from the time
Historians always disagree because the past cannot be known
b.why: Historians can reach different interpretations by choosing different sources, giving some more weight, or asking different questions. It does not mean one is careless. The option about always disagreeing is wrong because disagreement has causes that can be examined.
b.clue: Think about how historians build an interpretation from sources.

a.best: A historian's 2015 book arguing why a strike began

b.best: They may use different sources or weigh evidence differently

problems.detail: The right option is the only one hedged with 'may'. Every distractor uses an absolute ('always', 'Only', 'must'), so a test-savvy student can pick the answer without knowing the idea. Reword one or two distractors without absolutes.

opts: They may use different sources or weigh evidence differently
One of them is probably being careless with the evidence
One is giving a perspective and the other an interpretation
